linear_probing.description: Logistic probes trained on residual-stream activations decode the brand-preference signal from open-weight model layers, revealing that the preference is a linear feature in hidden states rather than an emergent behavioural quirk.
linear_probing.headline: 77 to 88 per cent classification accuracy reading brand-preferring vs spec-optimal hidden states.

activation_steering.description: Adding a brand-preference vector (multiplier alpha) to mid-layer activations at inference time produces a smooth dose-response in non-optimal-recommendation rate.
activation_steering.headline: 21-percentage-point swing in non-optimal recommendation across nine multiplier levels.

base_vs_instruct.description: Gemma 4 31B base model (no post-training) compared with the instruction-tuned release. RLHF moderates the preference but does not eliminate it; the signal remains decodable from hidden states.
base_vs_instruct.headline: Base 67 per cent → Instruct 20 per cent, but the preference is still linearly decodable.

brand_frequency_stability.description: Brand frequencies in pretraining corpora correlate strongly across the four major public datasets, so the training-data signal is stable regardless of which corpus a model was trained on.
brand_frequency_stability.headline: Cross-corpus Pearson 0.96–0.99 across 105 brands and four pretraining datasets.

inverse_scaling.description: Larger frontier models are MORE misaligned, not less. A linear regression on capability tier (small / mid / large frontier) yields a positive coefficient.
inverse_scaling.headline: Each capability tier raises the non-optimal rate by 10.8 percentage points (P = 5×10⁻⁴, R² = 0.36).

cross_provider.description: Model behaviour at the assortment level is highly correlated across providers, suggesting the same underlying training-data signal drives all systems.

control_accuracy.description: Across four control conditions, models score above 99% accuracy — proving the misalignment is not incompetence.

asymmetric_install_remove.description: Installing the brand preference requires very few examples; removing it requires many more. This creation–removal asymmetry is the central causal asymmetry in the paper.
asymmetric_install_remove.headline: 100 examples install Axelion preference at 52.5%; 500–6,000 examples are needed to wash it out.

thinking_ablation.description: Thinking variants reduce misalignment for small models but increase it for large models. The pattern complicates simple narratives about reasoning helping.

open_vs_proprietary.headline: Open-weight models (n=4) are slightly more misaligned at baseline than proprietary (n=20) but converge below 0.4–0.8 per cent at the explicit threshold.

vague_paradox.description: Twelve of thirty models actually INCREASE their non-optimal rate when moving from no specification to a vague preference — a direction-of-effect inversion.
vague_paradox.headline: 12 of 30 models recommend more non-optimally when given a vague preference than when given none.
